question.text: Two sitar strings, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>A</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>B</mi></math> playing the note '<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>D</mi><mi>h</mi><mi>a</mi></math>' are slightly out of tune and produce beats of frequency <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5</mn><mo> </mo><mi>Hz</mi></math>. The tension of the string <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>B</mi></math> is slightly increased and the beat frequency is found to decrease by <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>3</mn><mo> </mo><mi>Hz</mi></math>. If the frequency of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>A</mi></math> is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>425</mn><mo> </mo><mi>Hz</mi></math>. The original frequency of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>B</mi></math> is

solution.text: The frequency of B is either 420 Hz or 430 Hz. As, the tension in B is increased its frequency will increase. If the frequency is 430 Hz, the beat frequency will increase. If the frequency is 420 Hz beat frequency will decrease, hence the correct answer is 420 Hz.
